fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`caused_by` is the store's only machine-readable causation edge and it is not trustworthy:
`rebar link <bug> <target> caused_by` accepts ANY target, so `rebar metrics`
(`bug_caused_by_fan_in`) and the epic-close `caused_by` floor reason over edges nobody
validated. The most-linked target today is a misattribution whose "children" are unrelated
CI items.

Verified against `origin/main` first: `rebar link` validates only relation grammar, cycles,
the redundant-link guard and the closed-source guard (`graph/_links.py:add_dependency`), and
has NO `--force`. The "does a commit reference this ticket?" scan exists exactly once,
privately, as `_referencing_commits` in `_commands/close_precheck.py`; its `[]` return
conflates "scanned, none found" with "no git history".

## Approach

1. Hoist the trailer/subject scan into the existing shared module
   `_engine_support/commit_impact.py` as `referencing_commits(ids, tracker, repo_root)`
   returning `list[str] | None`, `None` = "git history unreadable" — the same `None`-vs-`[]`
   distinction `changed_paths` there already uses. `close_precheck._referencing_commits`
   becomes a thin `... or []` delegate KEEPING ITS NAME (a string monkeypatch target in
   `tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py`); `_referencing_commit_exists` — re-exported by
   `transition_close` and asserted directly in `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` — still
   delegates to it, so both keep their current contracts.
2. Add ONE predicate `caused_by_refusal(target_id, relation, tracker, code_root) -> str | None`
   in `_commands/link_revert.py`. BOTH `link_core` (the write) and `_link_dry_run` (the
   preview) call it: `_link_dry_run` does not route through `link_core`, so a shared
   predicate — not a shared code path — is what stops the preview drifting from the refusal.
3. The rule: for `caused_by`, the RESOLVED TARGET must have >=1 referencing commit — the
   target ITSELF, not its descendants, because `caused_by` must name the specific change that
   introduced the defect and crediting an epic through its children is the exact
   misattribution this story exists to stop. `caused_by` is never hierarchy-promoted, so the
   resolved target is the requested one.
4. Command layer, not `add_dependency`: `rebar.graph` is the store layer, runs NO git and
   takes no `repo_root` (only `tracker_dir`), and `link_core` is its only functional caller.
   Both callers resolve the CODE root as `config.repo_root(repo_root)` and pass THAT — never
   the tracker dir, which an absolute `tracker.dir` can relocate — mirroring close_precheck's
   `code_root`/`tracker` split.
5. Unverifiable is NOT invalid: `None` from the scan (no code repo / no commits) allows the
   link. A refusal must mean "this target has no commit", never "this clone has no history".
6. Escape hatch `--force[=<reason>]` on the CLI, `force=` on library and MCP, spelled as
   `claim --force`. Its parser moves to `_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:extract_force` and
   `claim._parse_force` delegates, so the CLAIM-STYLE spelling has one implementation shared
   by claim and link. `transition._extract_force` and `tracker_maintenance` keep theirs:
   transition's bare `--force` yields `''`, not `'(no reason given)'` — a different contract.
7. Reconciler: `_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:337` applies arbitrary
   inbound relations through `rebar.link` and fails open, so a peer-authored `caused_by` whose
   commit lives only in another clone would be dropped and recorded as an impossible link.
   That call passes `force="inbound reconcile: peer-authored edge"`; sync is unchanged.
8. Oracle: a `"link"` branch in `write_parity_contract.execute()` (and `Case.op`), plus `link`
   on the Adapter protocol and all three adapters changed from `(a, b, relation) -> None` to
   `(a, b, relation, *, force=None) -> Outcome`. `adapter.link` IS called, at
   `tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py:147` (`test_deps_parity`), which discards the
   return; that file joins Scope and gains `assert adapter.link(a, b, "blocks")`.
9. `SKILL.md`: the rule governs the `rebar link ... caused_by` form (CLI/library/MCP) ONLY —
   the close's `--caused-by=<id>` flag writes via `transition_close._apply_caused_by` and is
   NOT gated. Say that at the early-link instruction (~L598-607) AND at the Omission case
   (~L633-644), whose scope-of-work story/epic target is commit-less by construction, with
   the worked example `rebar link <bug> <story> caused_by --force="scope-of-work attribution:
   the story that should have covered this case has no introducing commit"` plus a note to
   repeat that reason in the RCA. Unattributable still leaves the link unset.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`,
`src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py`,
`src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt`, `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py`,
`src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`,
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`,
`tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py` (new), `tests/interfaces/adapters.py`,
`tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py`,
`docs/ticket-model.md`, `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`.

## Explicitly OUT of scope

The original plan's `introducing_sha` field + `rebar fsck` date check and the "attach the
196-row corpus" criterion are cut and re-filed as a follow-up linked `discovered_from`: no
surface writes `introducing_sha` so it would land dead; `fsck` is a STORE-integrity walker
that must run where no code repo exists; the corpus is absent from the repo.

## Testing

New `tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py`, over a store whose code repo has real
commits: happy path (a target carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer commit links); refusal (the
error names the target and `--force`; `show_ticket(...)["deps"]` unchanged); `force="..."`
records the edge; `relates_to`/`blocks` to the same target unaffected; a commit-less code
repo allows the link; `--dry-run` prints "Would reject" and writes nothing;
`close_precheck._referencing_commits` still resolves by name and still returns `[]`.

Pinning: `tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py`, `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py`,
`tests/unit/test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py`, `tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py`,
`tests/unit/test_close_gate_*.py`, `tests/unit/test_claim_*.py`,
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A `caused_by` link to a commit-less target is refused identically on library, CLI and
      MCP, `force` bypassing it on all three; two new `op="link"` rows make
      `pytest tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py -q` cover it.
- [x] The refusal names the target and the escape hatch, leaves the store unwritten, previews
      under `--dry-run`, and allows a commit-less code repo; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py -q`.
- [x] The scan has ONE implementation:
      `test $(grep -cE '%H%x1f' src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py) -eq 0`.
- [x] The delegate keeps its name:
      `test $(grep -cE '^def _referencing_commits' src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py) -eq 1`.
- [x] The close gate is behaviour-identical:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py tests/unit/test_transition_close.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py -q`.
- [x] Docs state the rule: `grep -q 'referencing commit' docs/ticket-model.md` (absent today).
- [x] SKILL.md carries the forced-link example:
      `test $(grep -c 'scope-of-work attribution' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md) -eq 1`.
- [x] Gates green: `make lint`; `make typecheck`;
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reporting `new=0 increased=0`.
